### 1. What Zentrix Sales is and who it is for

Zentrix Sales is a working tool for field sales forces, developed and distributed by GUUAO LLC through the app stores of Google — [Google Play](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/#download), for Android — and Apple — the App Store, for iPhone. The two versions are the same app and do the same things; where this document describes something that depends on the operating system, both are named, because they do not always match. Anyone can download it, but without an account it does nothing: credentials are created and handed over by the company that contracts the service, and the app does not allow accounts to be created and has no sign-up. It is not a consumer app.

There are two kinds of people whose data is processed, and they are worth separating. On one side the rep, an employee of the company that contracted Zentrix Sales, who uses it in the course of their job. On the other, that company's customers — the shops the rep visits — whose information the app downloads so that work can be done, and about whom visits, orders and payments are recorded.

Who is responsible for what. The information the app collects is sent to the management system of the company that contracted Zentrix Sales, which is where it lives and where that company keeps it in accordance with its own policies and with the law. That company decides what commercial data it loads and what it uses it for. GUUAO LLC provides the app and processes that information on that company's behalf, without using it for purposes of its own. For any question about this document or about what the app does on the phone, the point of contact is [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company).

The data processing described here forms part of the employment relationship between the rep and their employer, and rests on the employer's legitimate interest in organising, coordinating and verifying field sales activity.

That is why the app shows no consent dialog and offers no switches to turn data collection off. This is not an oversight: recording location during the working day, recording visits and reporting crashes automatically are the very purpose of the tool, not optional extras. A consumer app would ask permission; a working tool informs. This document is that information, and it is given to each rep along with their access credentials.

Permissions are still requested by the phone's own operating system — Android or iOS, depending on the device — and the rep grants or denies them there; what does not exist is an additional consent layer inside the app. There are three, and they are the same on both systems: location, camera and notifications. The app does not request photo library access: when the rep picks a saved image, they do so in the system's own picker, which hands over that image and nothing else (clause 2.b).

Change note. Until 11 September 2026 Zentrix Sales existed only for Android, and this document was written that way: it named Android where it really meant “the phone's operating system”. That day the iPhone version appeared and the policy was revised in full to tell the two apart. Every clause that changed carries its own note — they are this one, 2.e, 2.g, 2.i, 2.j, 4 and 5.

What data is collected and what for did not change, and the two exceptions are stated where they belong: on the iPhone the notification additionally passes through Apple's infrastructure (clause 2.j) and, the other way round, the barcode reader stops sending technical data to Google (clause 2.i). Two things changed in this paragraph in particular: permissions are no longer “still requested by Android”, and “photo access” was removed from the list — that was never accurate, because neither version requests that permission.

### 2. What data we collect and why

### a) Geographic location (precise)

Zentrix Sales records the phone's position in two distinct situations, and they are worth separating because they are not the same thing:

- On starting (check-in) and closing (check-out) each customer visit, and when putting the order together, along with the accuracy of the reading and the time.

- During the working day, periodically, only while the app is open. With the app on screen, a point is taken every five minutes, which is the default interval: the company can change it from its system, and the app never takes more than one point a minute. With the app closed or in the background, none is taken: the only thing that happens on waking in the background is sending the points already taken. For each point, the position, the accuracy, the time and the company being worked with are stored. Battery level is not recorded with the route, nor whether the screen is on: that would measure the person and not the work. (A crash report, described in clause 2.h, does carry the phone's battery level at that moment, as technical data for diagnosing it; it does not travel with the route.)

What for: to record that the visit to each customer happened, where it happened and how long it lasted, and to let sales supervision follow field activity over the course of the day.

Who sees it: sales supervision and authorized staff at the company, inside their management system.

Nature: the location permission is required in order to record orders and payments: without it the app will not let them be made, and explains what is missing. If the permission is not granted or the phone's location service is off, the periodic recording simply does not happen, and the app does not make up for it in any other way. If in one particular shop the device cannot get a fix, the rep can carry on with the visit regardless.

Change note. Until 1 September 2026 this clause said that Zentrix Sales did not track the rep's route between visits, and on that date it was true. From that day the periodic recording described above became part of the app, by the company's decision, and this clause was rewritten to say so. The notice the app shows on screen was updated in the same move. On 2 September 2026 recording with the app closed was withdrawn, and this clause went back to saying only what the app does: position is taken only while the app is in use.

### b) Photographs

On each visit the rep may attach up to five photographs, taken with the phone's camera on the spot. They are resized on the phone itself before being sent and lose the camera metadata, including the coordinate the device embeds in the file. If the visit leaves a return, up to five photographs of the returned goods may also be attached, likewise from the camera only and with the same treatment.

What for: to leave evidence of the state of the point of sale, the product display, the stock or any incident.

Nature: optional. A visit closes with no photographs at all.

The visit photograph comes only from the camera: the app does not allow it to be picked from the gallery, so that an image from another day cannot pass for today's evidence.

There are three cases where an image may come from the phone's gallery, and in all three the rep picks it: the receipt for a payment — and the additional photographs accompanying it (clause 2.e) — because these are usually screenshots of a bank transfer; the rep's own profile photograph (clause 2.g); and the attachments to a chat with the back office (clause 2.k). In each one the app reads only the image picked, and never goes through the gallery on its own.

### c) The customer's handwritten signature

At the signature step, the customer can sign with a finger on the screen. The signature is stored as an image.

What is stored is the image and nothing else: the vector stroke, the pressure, the speed and the timing of the gesture are not kept.

What for: to record the customer's agreement with the order as taken.

Nature: optional.

### d) Information about the company's customers

The app downloads from the company's systems the customer list assigned to each rep: name or business name, tax ID, address, telephone, delivery addresses, shop coordinates, applicable price list, credit limit and availability, and unpaid invoices.

This information belongs to the company, is not generated by the app, and is held on the phone solely so that the rep can work offline. The app does not send it back as such: when it sends an order or a visit, it identifies the customer by their internal number in the company's system, not by their details. The exception is collections: with each payment go the balances of the customer's invoices that the rep had in front of them (clause 2.e). They go to the same company system they came from, not to third parties.

What is sent is what the rep produces during the visit: the order lines, the stock count, the returns and any free-text notes they write. Because those notes are an open field, they may contain a customer's name or address if the rep writes them there.

### e) Customer payment data

When a rep records a payment request, the amount, the date, the bank or journal, the bank reference and, if attached, the image of the receipt are sent. They may also attach up to three additional photographs — the rest of the transfers, the change, whatever is needed to support the payment — which stay in the chat for that request (clause 2.k). If they write a comment, that text stays in that same chat.

Each payment request also carries the balances the rep had in front of them when collecting: the list of the customer's invoices with their number and their balance in dollars, which of them the rep touched in that payment, the sum of those balances and the time those balances were read. They let whoever approves the request know what debt the payment was made against.

Separately from the payment, from an invoice the rep can record the customer's payment commitment — the date they promised to pay and, if they said it, the amount — and change that invoice's tags.

All of this goes only to the company's servers, to the same system the invoices came from. It is not sent to any third party.

Change note. The balances and the payment commitment have been named since 23 September 2026. The app was already sending them; this clause did not say so, and clause 2.d stated that customer information was not sent back.

Change note. The additional photographs were added on 11 September 2026. Until that day a payment request allowed a single image, the receipt, and this clause named only that one.

### f) Requests to add or correct customers

The rep cannot create or modify a customer record: what they can do is propose an addition or a correction, which someone at the company then approves or rejects. With that proposal travel the details the rep typed — name or business name, tax ID, telephone, address — and, in the case of an addition, the supporting documents the company's checklist requires, photographed at the shop and converted to PDF inside the phone. Among those documents are identity and tax papers belonging to the customer or their representative.

On converting the photographs to PDF, the app strips their metadata. A supporting document can also be a PDF the rep already has on the phone — for instance, one the customer sent them by messaging — picked in the operating system's own file picker. That PDF, of up to 1 MB, travels as it is: the app does not modify it, so it carries whatever metadata it came with (author, program, dates). None of these proposals writes anything into the company's systems by itself.

### g) The rep's account data

Email address and password on signing in, and the name they go by in the company's system. The password is transmitted in order to authenticate and is not stored on the phone. Session credentials are stored in the operating system's secure storage — the Keystore on Android, the Keychain on the iPhone — not in the app's database.

The app also has a local lock PIN, of the same kind as a banking app's. That PIN never leaves the phone: it does not travel to any server and is not stored in the clear, only its cryptographic hash inside the secure storage. If the rep picks a profile photograph, that photograph is stored on the phone and sent to the company's systems.

Change note. Until 11 September 2026 this clause named only the Android Keystore, because Zentrix Sales existed only for Android. The iPhone Keychain was added, which is the same mechanism on the other side. What is stored did not change.

### h) Operational diagnostics and crash reports

When the app fails, freezes or closes unexpectedly, this is recorded automatically: date and time, type of error, the error message, the first lines of the technical trace, the phone's operating system version, the device model and the last screens the user went through. On a reduced sample of sessions, performance measurements are also recorded (how long the app took to start or to sync) along with the list of network requests made, without their content.

Each report also carries the phone's technical context that the diagnostics service itself collects, depending on what each system supplies: manufacturer and model, free memory and storage, battery level and whether it is charging, screen orientation, connection type (Wi-Fi or mobile data), language and time zone, and whether the operating system has been modified (rooted). And it carries some tags of the app's own, so the failure can be classified: the number of the company being worked with, the subdomain of the company's server and the version of its system, whether the phone had signal at that moment, and the store the app was installed from.

This information travels by two routes: to the company's servers and to an external software diagnostics provider (see clause 4).

What is stripped before it goes to the external provider: the app automatically filters the text going out and replaces with generic tags anything that looks like an email address, a telephone number, an identity or tax number, geographic coordinates or a sum of money. No screenshots are attached, nor the screen's element tree, nor the content of server requests. The phone's IP address is not stored in the report, but the provider sees it on receiving it, like any server, and uses it to note the approximate city and country it came from: that does stay in the report. Of the rep's identity, only their internal employee number is sent, never their name or their email address.

And what that filter cannot strip, said plainly: it works by recognizing shapes — what looks like an email address, a phone number, an ID number, a coordinate or an amount — and a personal name or an address written in prose has no shape that tells it apart from the rest of the text. If an error message drags along what the rep wrote in a free-text note, that text may reach the diagnostics provider as it stands. That is why this policy declares — and the app store listing does too — that a customer's name and address may be shared by this route, even though the app never sends them deliberately.

And since version 5.2.11 there is a second route, which the rep opens themselves: the «Report a problem» form (Profile › About). It has a single field, free text, where the rep says what happened to them; on sending it, that text travels together with the same technical data described above — version, model, operating system, last screens, the phone's context, the tags and the internal employee number. It does not ask for the rep's name or email address, attaches no screenshots and sends nothing until «Send report» is tapped.

What is written in that field goes through the same filter and has the same limit as the previous paragraph: a name or an address written in prose cannot be told apart from the rest of the text. It is, in fact, the place where they are most likely to appear, because it is the rep who does the writing. It is best to say what happened and with which customer by their code, not by their name.

What for: to diagnose and fix failures. Before this channel existed, crashes in the field were only known about if the rep wrote them down by hand in a note.

Change note. This clause was updated on 23 September 2026, the day the app introduced the «Report a problem» form. Neither the categories of data nor the recipients change: what that form sends is what this same clause already described, and it goes to the same provider, with the same filtering and the same retention period. What changes is who triggers it — before, only a failure; now, the rep too — and that the text is written by a person, which is the case where the filter's limit weighs most.

Change note. That same day the list of what travels was also corrected: the phone's technical context, the app's tags and the approximate city and country were already being sent, and this clause did not name them; and it said the IP address was not sent without making clear what the provider deduces from it.

Nature: the automatic crash reporting is mandatory and cannot be switched off from the app. The «Report a problem» form is voluntary: it only sends something if the rep writes it and sends it.

### i) Technical data from the barcode reader

To read product barcodes, each version of the app uses its operating system's library, and that changes who receives what. On both, the code is read entirely inside the phone: neither the image captured by the camera nor the code read leaves the device.

- On Android it is ML Kit, a Google library, and it is the one that sends the technical data described below.

- On the iPhone it is Vision, the library belonging to Apple's own operating system. It works inside the device and sends nothing to anyone: by this route not one piece of technical data leaves the iPhone, neither to Google nor to Apple.

On Android only, that library sends Google, on its own account, technical data about its own operation: the phone's model and manufacturer, its operating system version, the name and version of this app, a technical identifier specific to the installation, response times, the configuration the library was invoked with, and any error codes produced.

What for, according to Google: to measure the performance of its libraries, debug them, maintain them and detect misuse.

Nature: mandatory on Android. That transmission is made by Google's own library and cannot be switched off from the app; the only alternative would be to remove barcode reading altogether. On the iPhone there is no transmission to switch off.

Change note. Until 11 September 2026 this clause said, without distinguishing, that the app uses ML Kit and that this library transmits technical data to Google. That was true, because the only version was the Android one. That day the iPhone version appeared, which reads codes with Apple's library and makes no such transmission, and the clause was split in two so as not to attribute to the iPhone a transfer that does not happen.

### j) Registering the phone to receive alerts (notifications)

Zentrix Sales tells the rep about things that happen when they are not looking at the screen: that an order was confirmed or canceled, that a payment request was approved or sent back, that a customer was assigned to them or taken away, or a message from the company. For an alert to reach a particular phone, that phone has to be registered first. That registration is what is described here.

What is sent and to whom. There are two transmissions and they go to different places:

- To Google — and, on the iPhone, to Apple as well. On starting up, the app asks Google's notification service — Firebase Cloud Messaging — for a registration token: a long string that identifies this installation of Zentrix Sales on this phone and which is the only thing that makes it possible to deliver an alert to the right device. In doing so, that service also generates, on its own account, a technical identifier for the installation, of the same kind as the one described in clause 2.i. On the iPhone there is one more step, because iOS admits no other route: before that, the device obtains from Apple its own token — that of the Apple Push Notification service — and it is that one Google needs in order to be able to deliver an alert to that iPhone.

- To the company's servers. The app then hands them that token, so an alert can be directed to this rep. Traveling with it are: a phone identifier of the app's own, generated at random the first time and kept in the operating system's secure storage; the platform name (android or ios, depending on the device); the version of Zentrix Sales installed; and a device tag (the operating system version and build), which is what makes it possible to know which phone to look at when a rep reports that nothing is reaching them.

About the app's own phone identifier: it is a random number created inside the device, does not come from the hardware or from any user account — neither the Google one on Android nor the Apple one on the iPhone — and identifies the phone, not the person: that is why it survives signing out, and why it also accompanies the rest of the requests the app makes to the company's servers. It is deleted when the app is uninstalled.

What is not sent in that registration: neither the rep's name nor their email address — the session already says whose phone it is — nor location, nor any customer data.

The text of every alert passes through Google, and on the iPhone it passes through Apple as well. It is written by the company's system and, to reach the phone, it crosses the notification service's infrastructure: Google's in both cases and, when the destination is an iPhone, Apple's on the last leg. It is the same route by which any notification reaches that phone, and there is no other: an alert that does not go through there does not arrive.

Nature: the rep can deny the notifications permission from their phone's settings — on Android or on the iPhone alike — and will then see no alerts. It is worth being precise: the phone is registered regardless, because that is part of how the app works and not of how alerts are presented. On signing out, the app deregisters, so that alerts about one customer list do not keep arriving at a phone that has changed hands.

Change note. This clause was updated on 11 September 2026, the day alerts started reaching the iPhone too. Two things change and are worth saying: the platform name traveling in the registration is no longer always android, and on the iPhone the alert crosses, in addition to Google's infrastructure, that of Apple — which previously played no part. What is sent and what for did not change.

### k) Chats with the back office

An order, a payment request, a customer or an invoice has, in the company's management system, a chat — the same message thread the back office sees — and the rep can read it and write in it from the app. What is sent is what the rep writes and picks: the message text, the mentions of people at the company that they themselves flag, and the attachments they decide to add — a photograph taken on the spot, an image from the gallery, or a PDF put together by photographing pages. Attachments are resized if they are too heavy, are sent only with a connection, and none travels without the rep having picked it one by one.

Where it is stored: in the company's management system, alongside the document it belongs to, just like everything else the app sends (clause 4). The rep sees only the chats for their own documents and for the customers on their list; an internal back-office note is visible to them only if they are mentioned in it.

On the phone: so it can be read offline, the app keeps an encrypted copy of the first page of every chat the rep has opened — along with the list of people who can be mentioned in it — inside the same local database described in clause 4, and when showing it, says how old that copy is. A message written with no signal waits on the phone and goes out by itself when the signal comes back.

Change note. This clause was added on 2 September 2026, the day chats arrived in the app.

### l) App usage (product measurement)

Since version 5.2.1, the app measures how it is used with Google Analytics for Firebase, from Google LLC. It sends two things: which screens are opened, by their generic name (for instance, «/pedidos» or «/factura»), and a closed list of about thirty usage events — that a visit was opened or closed, that the barcode reader was used, that a payment was recorded, that someone signed in, that a submission went to the queue or was rejected, among others.

What each event carries: only counts, whole numbers such as how many orders, lines, photographs or invoices that visit or that payment had. The app discards any other data before sending it: no name, email address, telephone, tax ID or address travels, no coordinate, no amount or balance, nor the number of a customer, an order or an invoice. A screen's name is trimmed so that it never carries an identifier. The rep's employee number is not sent either.

What Google adds on its own account: as in any app using that service, each transmission carries a technical installation identifier generated by the library itself, the phone model, the operating system and app versions, the language, and the approximate city and country Google deduces from the connection. The library also records, by itself, the first use, the start of each session and the time in use.

No advertising identifier: collection of the advertising identifier is switched off on both versions — on Android, the permission that would provide it is also removed — and what is measured is not used to personalize ads. That is why the app does not request iOS's tracking permission.

What for: to know which parts of the app are used and where reps get stuck, in order to decide what to improve.

Nature: always sent, and it cannot be switched off from the app.

Change note. This clause was added on 23 September 2026. The measurement has existed since version 5.2.1, of 16 September 2026, and until today this policy said, wrongly, that the app used no analytics tools and no external product analytics provider.

### 3. What we do NOT do

Zentrix Sales does not:

- show advertising or contain any advertising library;

- use user profiling or marketing tracking tools. It does measure how the app is used (clause 2.l), but that measurement counts screens and events, with no personal data and no advertising identifier;

- collect any advertising identifier: neither Android's advertising ID nor Apple's (IDFA) on the iPhone — the app does not even request the tracking permission iOS requires for that;

- access contacts, the microphone, messages, the calendar or the call history;

- sell, rent or transfer data to third parties for commercial purposes;

- create automated profiles producing legal effects on people.

On identifiers: the diagnostics tool described in clause 2.h, the barcode-reading library described in clause 2.i — on Android only —, the notification service described in clause 2.j and the usage measurement described in clause 2.l each generate a technical identifier specific to each installation, and the app itself also generates its own to identify the phone to the company's servers. All are random numbers created on the phone, which do not come from the device or from any account, and serve to group the records of one device together. They are not used for advertising, are not shared with advertisers, and disappear when the app is uninstalled.

### 4. Where the data is stored

On the phone: the app keeps an encrypted local database so work can go on offline, holding the customer list, prices, visit drafts, location points not yet sent, photographs and signatures awaiting despatch, and the copy of the chats the rep has opened (clause 2.k). This database is excluded from cloud backup — neither Google's on Android nor iCloud's on the iPhone — so that the company's information does not reach the employee's personal account. On Android it is also excluded from the direct transfer of data when changing phones. And, on both systems, the key that decrypts that database is stored in such a way that it travels in no backup and to no other device: a database without its key cannot be read. Each rep has their own: on a shared phone, one does not see a single row of the other's.

A caveat about photographs, the signature and supporting documents: while a visit or a customer addition is still open, those files are stored as loose files in the storage the operating system reserves for the app, outside the encrypted database and unencrypted, so that a draft does not lose them if the system closes the app. That storage is also excluded from cloud backup. When the visit is closed, the photographs and the signature move into the send queue, inside the encrypted database, and those loose files are deleted.

On the company's servers: all synced information — visits, orders, routes, photographs, signatures, payment requests, customer requests and the messages and attachments from chats — is sent to the management system of the company that contracted Zentrix Sales, where it is integrated with the rest of its commercial information. That system is its own: the app keeps no parallel copy anywhere else.

External diagnostics provider: the crash reports and performance measurements described in clause 2.h are additionally processed in Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.), a software diagnostics service whose receiving servers are in the United States. That entails an international transfer of that diagnostic data, limited to what is described in that clause and with the filtering explained there. Sentry acts as a processor on the company's behalf and is not authorized to use that information for any purpose of its own. No external advertising provider is used.

Usage measurement: the events and screens described in clause 2.l are sent to Google LLC through Google Analytics for Firebase, with receiving servers in the United States: this too is an international transfer, limited to what is described in that clause. Google processes that information under the terms of that service; the app has advertising-identifier collection and ad-personalization signals switched off.

Barcode-reading library (on Android only): the technical data described in clause 2.i is transmitted to Google LLC, whose receiving servers are in the United States, which likewise entails an international transfer, limited to that technical data. Google uses it to maintain and improve its own libraries, in accordance with its terms of use. Neither the camera images nor the codes read are transmitted. On the iPhone this transfer does not exist: there the reading is done by the operating system's own library, inside the device.

Notification service: the registration described in clause 2.j is handled by Google LLC through Firebase Cloud Messaging, with receiving servers in the United States: this too is an international transfer. Passing by that route are the phone's registration token, the technical installation identifier the service itself generates and the text of every alert, which is what has to be delivered. Google is involved here in order to get the alert to the right phone, and is not authorized to use that information for any purpose of its own beyond providing that service.

Apple's notification service (on the iPhone only): iOS does not allow an alert to arrive by any route but its own, so on the iPhone the last leg is handled by Apple Inc. through the Apple Push Notification service, with receiving servers in the United States: this too is an international transfer. Passing by that route are the registration token Apple assigns to that iPhone and the text of every alert. Apple is involved, like Google, solely to deliver the alert to the right device.

Maps: the screens that show a map — a customer's record, the detail of one of their branches, and the one where the rep confirms where the shop is — download their imagery from OpenStreetMap, a free public service: they request it from tile.openstreetmap.org, operated by the OpenStreetMap Foundation, based in the United Kingdom. Requesting a map tile reveals, to whoever serves it, the phone's IP address and the area being looked at, which on a customer's record is the area where their shop is. That is why the map is drawn only on those detail screens, never in a list, and never in advance: a map the rep has not opened is not downloaded.

Change note. Until 6 September 2026 the map was drawn on a single screen, and this clause said so. That day, by the company's decision, it also began to be drawn on the customer record and on the detail of their branches. Who it is shared with did not change — it is still the same public service — but how many times did: the clause was corrected on 11 September 2026, when it was reviewed in full. On 23 September 2026 it was corrected again: it said no data about the rep or the customer traveled by this route, and the area being looked at and the phone's IP address do reach whoever serves the map.

«Ir con Google Maps» (Go with Google Maps): that button opens the phone's maps app to get to the customer's shop — Google Maps if it is installed; if not, whichever the phone has, which on the iPhone is Apple Maps — and hands it the shop's coordinates and, depending on the case, the customer's name and address. It only happens when the rep taps it. What that app then does with that data depends on its own policy.

Transmission: all of the app's communications take place exclusively over HTTPS. The app is configured to reject any unencrypted connection.

An external service, with no personal data: to show the reference exchange rate, the app queries public sources for the exchange rate in Venezuela. Those queries carry no data about the user or the customer: they include no credentials, no identifiers and no content at all.

### 5. For how long

On the phone: route points already sent to the server are deleted automatically seven days after being sent. Everything else that went out through the send queue — photographs and signatures included — is deleted from the phone once sent, as soon as it is more than seven days old counting from when it was recorded (not from when it was sent). Anything not yet sent is kept until the sync is confirmed, so as not to lose the rep's work.

On signing out, the credentials are removed from the device; the rep's local database stays, encrypted, precisely so as not to lose what has not gone out yet. The app itself allows it to be viewed and wiped under Manage accounts on this phone, on the sign-in screen, saying first how many pending submissions would be lost. When the app is uninstalled, the phone deletes its local files, the encrypted database included.

Change note. Until 11 September 2026 this sentence named Android, which was the only system Zentrix Sales existed on. It was rewritten so that it holds on both.

On the company's servers: information is kept for as long as the applicable accounting, tax and labour obligations in Venezuela require, and in any event while the associated tax obligation has not lapsed. Visits, photographs and signatures form part of the commercial document they belong to — the order, the payment request, the visit record — and are kept alongside it and for the same length of time: they have no shorter period of their own. Route points have a period of their own, a shorter one: the management system deletes them automatically ninety (90) days after they were taken, with a purging task that runs every night. Ninety days is the default value; the company can change it from its system's settings. It is the same period the notice the app shows on screen states.

Change note. Until 23 September 2026 this paragraph said that purging ships switched off and was not switched on, and that route points were therefore kept with no set period. The first part is true — it ships switched off — but on the company's system it was already switched on: the paragraph was corrected to state the period actually applied.

At the diagnostics provider: crash reports and performance measurements are kept for thirty (30) days, which is the period configured in that service, and are then deleted.

On the retention period for photographs and signatures: announcing an early deletion for them, shorter than that of the document they form part of, was considered and decided against. They are the evidence that the visit happened and that the customer agreed, and separating them from the document they support would leave it without evidential value exactly when it is needed. Announcing a period that is then not applied would be worse than announcing none.

### 6. Who it is shared with

Inside the company: the information Zentrix Sales collects is transmitted to the management system of the company that contracted the service, and only authorized staff (sales supervision, administration and IT) have access to it in the exercise of their duties. On GUUAO LLC's side, access is limited to the technical staff strictly needed to operate and support the app.

Outside the company, only with the providers identified in clause 4 — the software diagnostics provider; Google, for the notification service, for usage measurement and, on Android, for the barcode-reading library; Apple, on the iPhone, for the last leg of that same notification service; and the OpenStreetMap Foundation, for the map imagery — and limited in each case to what is described there. No other category of information — location, photographs, signatures, orders, customer or payment data — is transmitted to third parties, with these caveats, worth stating clearly rather than leaving implicit:

- the phone's approximate city and country, which the diagnostics provider and Google deduce from the connection on receiving a report or a usage event (clauses 2.h and 2.l);

- the area looked at on the map, which reaches OpenStreetMap when its imagery is requested and which, on a customer's record, is the area of their shop (clause 4);

- the shop's coordinates, and sometimes the customer's name and address, which the «Ir con Google Maps» button hands to the phone's maps app when the rep taps it (clause 4);

- the text of a crash report may drag along whatever the rep wrote in a free-text note, and a customer's name or address may appear there (clause 2.h);

- the text of an alert crosses Google's infrastructure and, if the destination is an iPhone, Apple's too, because that is the only way for it to reach the phone (clause 2.j).

Information may only be disclosed to other third parties where a competent authority requires it under Venezuelan law.

The website. This policy is about the app. The site zentrix.company, which you are probably reading it on, shows no advertising and only measures visits with Google Analytics if the visitor accepts it in the cookie notice; without that permission it sets no cookies and loads nothing from Google. What is measured and how to withdraw permission is in [Cookies and analytics](https://zentrix.company/en/privacy/#cookies). Like any website, it is served by a hosting provider (GitHub, with Cloudflare in front), which sees the connection's IP address in order to deliver the page.

One exception that depends on the rep: the app can generate an order note as a PDF — including the customer's name, the order lines, the prices, the total and, where there was one, their signature — and send it from the phone itself through the apps installed (messaging, for instance). That sending is decided and carried out by the rep, and its destination is outside the app's control. The company instructs its staff to share that document only with the customer it belongs to.

### 7. Rights: access, correction and deletion

Anyone whose data is processed through Zentrix Sales — reps and the company's customers — may request access, correction or deletion of their data by writing to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company), putting Data request — Zentrix Sales in the subject line and supplying enough information to identify themselves.

The request will be answered within a maximum of thirty (30) business days. Deletion may be limited where retention is necessary to meet legal, accounting or tax obligations, or to defend claims; in that case the reason and the period will be stated.

Signing out does not delete data from the server: it only removes the credentials from the phone. To delete data, use the channel above.

### 8. Minors

Zentrix Sales is aimed exclusively at adults working as field sales reps for one of the companies that contract it. Although the app downloads freely from Google Play and from the App Store, without an account issued by one of those companies there is nothing to use. It is not intended for minors and does not knowingly collect data about minors.

### 9. Security

Session credentials are stored in the operating system's encrypted storage. The app's local database is encrypted, and its key lives in that same protected storage on the phone; the photographs, signature and supporting documents of a visit or a customer addition still open are kept separately, without that encryption (clause 4). The app communicates exclusively over HTTPS. Local data is excluded from cloud backup and from device-to-device transfer. The app locks itself with a local PIN after fifteen minutes of inactivity. Server access is restricted to authorized staff.

No security measure is absolute. The company works continuously on strengthening the protection of the information held on devices.

### 10. Changes to this policy

Any amendment will be published at this same address with a new update date. Substantial changes will additionally be communicated to reps through the company's internal channels and will be reflected in the notice the app itself shows on screen.

Change note (23 September 2026). This policy was checked against what the app does, and what it failed to say or said wrongly was corrected: usage measurement with Google Analytics for Firebase (new clause 2.l, and the denials in clauses 3 and 4); the invoice balances that reach the company with each payment, and the payment commitment recorded on an invoice (2.d and 2.e); the retention of the route on the company's system, which is deleted after ninety days and not kept with no set period (5); OpenStreetMap and the «Ir con Google Maps» button as third parties (4 and 6); what the diagnostics provider actually receives (2.h); that the photographs, signature and supporting documents of open work sit outside the encrypted database (4 and 9); and details of the route, return photographs, PDF supporting documents and the send queue (2.a, 2.b, 2.f and 5). Nothing changed in the app that day: what changed is that the policy now says it.

Change note (13 October 2026). The app was renamed Zentrix Sales, and this policy moved from vendooapp.com/en/privacy.html to zentrix.company/en/sales/privacy/. What is collected, why, and who it is shared with did not change. The website paragraph (clause 6) was rewritten, because the new site uses no analytics and no contact form.

GUUAO LLC [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company)

## [Terms of service — Zentrix Sales](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/terms/)

Terms of service of Zentrix Sales, the field sales app for Android and iPhone: who contracts it, who uses it every day and which rules apply.

Legal

### Zentrix Sales terms of service

This is a courtesy translation. The binding version of this document is the Spanish one, at [vendooapp.com/terminos.html](https://zentrix.company/sales/terminos/). If the two texts disagree, the Spanish text prevails. It is translated so you can read it, not to create a second binding text: these clauses are written on Venezuelan law, and clauses 15 and 17 turn on it.

Application

Zentrix Sales (com.leiros.vendoo), Android 7.0 or later and iOS 15 or later.

Owner

GUUAO LLC

Download

Google Play (Android) and the App Store (iPhone). [Both links are on the Zentrix Sales page](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/#download).

Contact

[hola@zentrix.company](mailto:hola@zentrix.company)

Published

2 September 2026

Last updated

13 October 2026

Contents

- Purpose and scope

- Who may use Zentrix Sales

- The account, the password and the PIN

- Permitted and prohibited use

- The information belongs to the company

### 1. Purpose and scope

These terms govern the use of Zentrix Sales, the app that GUUAO LLC (“the provider”) develops and distributes through [Google Play](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/#download), for Android, and the App Store, for iPhone. They govern both versions equally, which are the same app.

Zentrix Sales is a working tool for field sales forces. It is contracted by a distributor or any other organization with reps out on the street (“the company”) for its commercial staff, and the person using it every day is each of its sales reps (“the rep”). On signing in, the rep acknowledges having read this document and the [privacy policy](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/privacy/).

Anyone can download it, but without an account it does nothing. The app does not allow accounts to be created and has no sign-up: credentials are created and handed over by the company that contracted the service. Zentrix Sales is not a consumer app, and the rep's use of it forms part of their job: it does not constitute a consumer relationship between the rep and the provider.

The commercial relationship between the provider and the company that contracts Zentrix Sales is governed by the agreement the two of them sign. This document governs the use of the app.

Change note. Until 11 September 2026 Zentrix Sales existed only for Android, and this document named only that store and that operating system. That day the iPhone version appeared and the text was revised to cover both. No obligation and no right changed: what changed is which phones they apply to.

### 2. Who may use Zentrix Sales

Zentrix Sales may be used by a person to whom a client company has issued access credentials. Without them, the app shows nothing but the sign-in screen: there is no registration, no free trial and no guest mode.

Each rep's access is tied to their employment or contractual relationship with the company, and is withdrawn when that ends.

### 3. The account, the password and the PIN

Credentials are personal and non-transferable. The rep is responsible for keeping them private and for everything done from their session.

The app also requires a local lock PIN, set the first time you sign in and changeable under Profile › Account. That PIN protects the phone, not the account: it never leaves the device. For the same reason, there is no way to recover it: whoever forgets it has to sign out and sign back in with their password.

If the rep suspects their password has been exposed, or if they lose the phone, they must report it immediately through their company's channels.

### 4. Permitted and prohibited use

Zentrix Sales is used for the company's commercial work and nothing else. In particular, the rep undertakes not to:

- share their credentials or let another person use their session;

- extract, copy or circulate the customer list, prices, balances or any other company information beyond what their job requires;

- record visits, orders, payments or stock counts that do not correspond to real events;

- alter, decompile or attempt to bypass the app's controls, nor reach the company's systems by any route other than the app itself;

- use the app on a phone whose operating system has been modified in a way that compromises the protected storage where the credentials and the encrypted database live.

The order-note PDF includes customer details and their signature. It is shared only with the customer it belongs to.

### 5. The information belongs to the company

The customer list, prices, inventory, balances, invoices and everything else the app downloads are the information of the company that contracted Zentrix Sales, and are made available to the rep solely for the exercise of their duties. The same applies to what the rep produces with the app: orders, visits, photographs, notes, signatures and payment requests. The provider acquires no rights over that information: it carries it and holds it on the company's behalf.

The copy left on the phone is temporary and operational, so that work can go on offline. When the relationship with the company ends, the rep must sign out and, if the company instructs it, wipe the local data under Manage accounts on this phone.

### 6. Service availability and working offline

Zentrix Sales depends on the company's systems and on the phone's connection. Uninterrupted availability is not guaranteed, nor is any particular sync time: there may be maintenance, network outages or areas with no coverage.

The app is built for that. What the rep records with no signal is not lost: it is held on the phone and sent when the connection returns, even with the app closed. That said, it is worth putting precisely:

- A document being on the phone does not mean it is in the company's systems. The app distinguishes those states in those words — “To send”, “Could not send” — and the rep must look at them before treating a job as closed.

- If a submission is definitively rejected by the server, the app says so with its reason and does not retry. That document does not exist until it is corrected.

- It is the rep's responsibility to connect at least once a day, so their work arrives and so the information they are carrying — prices, balances, customer list — does not go stale.

### 7. Prices, quotes and order confirmation

This is the clause most worth understanding.

What the app shows before an order is sent is a quote, not a confirmed price. The price, the tax and the total are calculated by the company's system when it receives the order, at the rate in force on the day that order arrives. The phone carries a copy that may have gone stale through syncing late; in case of any discrepancy, the company's system prevails.

The quoted total travels with the order and is recorded separately, for two purposes: to be able to warn the rep if the amount changed on processing, and to be able to settle a customer's complaint about what they were quoted. It is not used to calculate anything.

An order recorded from the app is a commercial proposal. Its acceptance, dispatch and invoicing are governed by the company's commercial terms and remain subject to stock availability and to the customer's credit status.

### 8. Collections and payment requests

What the rep records in the app is a payment request that someone in administration reviews and approves afterwards. “Sent” does not mean “Approved”, and the app says so on every screen.

The rep is responsible for the accuracy of the amount, the bank reference, the journal and the receipt they attach, and for the safekeeping of any money they receive until it is handed over, in line with their company's internal procedures. A recorded request does not release the customer from their obligation until the company approves and applies it.

Where the amount collected exceeds what is applied to invoices, the difference is left as customer credit available. The app shows this before sending, so the rep can tell the customer there and then.

### 9. Requests to add or correct customers

The rep does not create or modify a customer record: they propose. Every addition and every correction is subject to approval by an authorized person at the company, and until then has no effect whatsoever.

The supporting documents the rep photographs are identity and tax documents belonging to third parties. They are collected solely to process that request, and the rep must obtain them with the customer's knowledge and must not keep them on their own outside the app.

### 10. Recording field activity

Zentrix Sales records work activity: the time and place of each visit, the route over the working day, the documents the rep produces and the app's failures. That record is the point of the tool, and it is described in detail, with its scope and its retention periods, in the [privacy policy](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/privacy/), which forms part of these terms.

The app explains all of this inside the app itself, before requesting any operating-system permission. The location permission is required in order to record orders and payments; without it those functions are unavailable.

### 11. The phone, mobile data and the battery

Zentrix Sales runs on the rep's phone or on the one their company assigns them, and uses mobile data to sync, including in the background.

The handset and the data plan are agreed between each company and its worker, outside this document: who provides the phone, who pays for the plan and on what terms is not decided by the app or by the provider.

What does depend on the app is using little, and it is built for that: everything is saved on the phone first and synced in batches, so that working with no signal is the normal case and there is no need to be permanently connected. Even so, for background sync to work, the operating system has to allow the app to wake up, and that decision is its own: on Android, the aggressive battery savers some manufacturers ship enabled can prevent it, and on the iPhone it is the system itself that decides when to grant that moment. Hence what is said above: what the rep records is not lost, but its being on the phone does not mean it has arrived, and the way to make sure is to open the app with a signal.

### 12. Intellectual property

Zentrix Sales, its name, its logo, its code and its design belong to GUUAO LLC. These terms transfer no rights over the app: they only authorize its use, on a limited, revocable and non-transferable basis, for as long as the company's contract and the rep's relationship with it last. The commercial information the company loads and produces with the app remains its own, in accordance with clause 5.

### 13. Privacy

The processing of personal data is described in the [privacy policy](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/privacy/), which is understood to form an integral part of these terms. It also contains the channel and the deadline for requesting access, correction or deletion.

### 14. Suspension and termination of access

The company may suspend or withdraw a rep's access at any time, in particular when the employment or contractual relationship ends, where there are signs of use contrary to clause 4, or for security reasons.

Termination of access does not by itself delete information already synced, which is retained in accordance with clause 5 of the privacy policy.

### 15. Liability

The provider makes Zentrix Sales available to the companies that contract it and to their staff, and undertakes to keep it running and to fix the faults reported to it, but does not warrant that the app is free of errors or available without interruption. Nor is it liable for failures of the mobile network, the operating system or the phone itself, or for use of the app contrary to these terms.

Each company is responsible for its own commercial decisions — prices, credit, dispatch, approval of payments and approval of new customers — which are taken in its own systems: the app carries information and proposes, it does not decide. The rep is responsible for the truthfulness of what they record and for the use they make of the company's information.

This clause does not limit any inalienable right of the worker, and cannot be read as a waiver. Under article 18 of the Organic Law of Labour and Male and Female Workers (LOTTT), labour rights are inalienable and any stipulation implying their waiver or diminution is void. Accordingly, nothing said here relieves the employer of its labour obligations, nor does it curtail the actions the law affords the rep against their employer. Neither is liability for wilful misconduct excluded, nor any other liability that Venezuelan law does not permit to be excluded.

### 16. Changes to these terms

The provider may amend these terms. The version in force is published at this same address with its date, and substantial changes are additionally communicated to client companies, which pass them on to their staff through their internal channels.

### 17. Governing law and disputes

These terms are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

In the event of any dispute arising from these terms or from use of the app, the parties shall first seek an amicable settlement, raised in writing to [hola@zentrix.company](mailto:hola@zentrix.company) and dealt with within thirty (30) consecutive days. If no agreement is reached within that period, the dispute shall be submitted to the competent courts of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela.

The above does not displace the labour jurisdiction: disputes between a rep and their employer arising from the employment relationship are governed by Venezuelan labour law and are heard before the competent labour courts, and nothing in this document may alter that.

### 18. Contact

GUUAO LLC [hola@zentrix.company](mailto:hola@zentrix.company)

Zentrix Sales

Odoo 19 implementation in Venezuela with the Venezuelan localization: SENIAT e-invoicing, IGTF, VAT and income-tax withholdings and Bs/USD at the BCV rate.

Solution

### Odoo® implementation with Venezuelan localization

We digitize your company from the inside: Odoo® adapted to Venezuela’s tax and operating reality, with unified processes and every resource under control.

[Ask for a proposal](mailto:hola@zentrix.company?subject=Zentrix%3A%20Odoo%20in%20Venezuela) [All solutions](https://zentrix.company/en/solutions/)

What’s included

### What we do, concretely.

### Technology
- Odoo®
- ERP
- Localización Venezuela

Venezuelan Odoo localization

### What it covers, module by module.

We run and maintain it in production on Odoo 19, at distribution and retail companies in Venezuela.

- 01

### SENIAT e-invoicing
Odoo sends every invoice, credit note and debit note to Soluciones Láser, an authorized digital-invoicing provider, which assigns its control number.

- 02

### IGTF in Odoo
The 3% IGTF tax is applied only to payments in foreign currency, in invoicing and at the point of sale.

- 03

### VAT and income-tax withholdings
VAT (IVA) and income-tax (ISLR) withholding vouchers with a preview before they are issued, plus the municipal business tax.

- 04

### Purchase and sales books
The legal purchase and sales books, with the VAT summary by rate for the tax return.

- 05

### Bolívars and dollars at the BCV rate
Every document in both currencies at the BCV rate, with exchange differences and reports in bolívars and dollars.

- 06

### Fiscal printer at the point of sale
Odoo Point of Sale prints on HKA and Bixolon fiscal printers, with IGTF on foreign-currency payments.

- 07

### Numbering and branches
Invoice number, control number and delivery notes, with each document tied to its branch.

- 08

### Venezuelan payroll (LOTTT)
Severance, vacations, profit sharing and settlements under the LOTTT labor law, the bank file and the ISLR ARC form.

Frequently asked questions

### Odoo in Venezuela, plainly.

### Does Odoo issue SENIAT digital invoices?
Yes. With the localization, Odoo sends every invoice, credit note and debit note to Soluciones Láser, an authorized digital-invoicing provider, which assigns the control number.

### How does Odoo handle the IGTF tax?
Odoo applies the 3% IGTF only when the payment is in foreign currency, both on invoices and at the point of sale.

### Can Odoo run in bolívars and dollars?
Yes. Every document is recorded in both currencies at the BCV rate, with exchange differences and reports in bolívars and dollars.

### Does Odoo Point of Sale work with a fiscal printer?
Yes. It prints on HKA and Bixolon fiscal printers, with IGTF on foreign-currency payments.

### Which Odoo version do you implement?
Odoo 19, the version our localization runs on in production today.

## [Support — Questions, access and your data | Zentrix](https://zentrix.company/en/support/)

Zentrix Work and Zentrix Sales support: common questions, access, manuals and how to delete your account or your data. A person replies within one business day.

Support

### How can we help?

Common questions, access, manuals and your data for every Zentrix app, in one place. If you can’t find it, a person replies within one business day.

Search the site Search

### Pick your product

- Work
- Sales
- Check

- [Traza (opens in a new tab)](https://traza.technology)

Delete your account: Zentrix Work · Delete your account: Zentrix Sales · Delete your account: Zentrix Check

### Zentrix Work
Store teams · [Zentrix Work →](https://zentrix.company/en/work/)

For almost everything, your first point of contact is your store manager: they set up your account, enable your tasks and can cut off access if you lose your phone. For anything else, write to us.

[soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company?subject=Support%20%E2%80%94%20Zentrix%20Work)

Put Support — Zentrix Work in the subject line and tell us the email you use in the app, your store and what happened. If you can, add a screenshot.

### Quick questions

### I don’t have an account. How do I sign up?
There is no sign-up: the app is only for the staff of companies that use Zentrix Work, and your manager creates your account. If you are a customer of the store, what you are looking for is that company’s customer app.

### I forgot my PIN
On the PIN screen, tap Forgot your PIN? You sign in again with your email and password and create a new PIN. You don’t lose your shift or any work you had in progress.

### I forgot my password
It is the same password as your company account. Ask your manager to reset it, or write to us.

### My orders don’t make a sound
Make sure you are clocked in at a store: when you are clocked out, the app never makes a sound. If you are clocked in, check that notifications for Zentrix Work are allowed and that the phone is not on “Do Not Disturb.” When you clock in, the app warns you if any of that is wrong.

### It won’t let me clock in
The server checks that you are at the store, that you have permission there and that the task is enabled. The message on screen tells you which of those failed. If you think it is a mistake, tell your manager.

### My shift ended on its own
This happens when the app has not heard from you for a long time: the phone has no signal or the app has not been used. It is on purpose, so your phone doesn’t keep ringing if you have left. Clock in again and carry on.

### I lost my phone or got a new one
Let your manager know so they can close your access on the old phone. On the new one, install the app and sign in with your email and password. What the app stored on the old phone is not copied to the new one, on purpose.

### I no longer work at the company
Your access is closed from the company’s system and the app stops working on your phone. You can uninstall it. To ask for your data to be deleted, see delete your account or your data.

### Manual

The [operator manual](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/) (in Spanish) explains shifts, orders, picking, delivery and returns step by step.

### Delete your account or your data — Zentrix Work

The app does not let you create accounts, so they are not deleted from it either: your company creates the account and your company closes it. To ask for this:

- Write to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company?subject=Data%20request%20%E2%80%94%20Zentrix%20Work) with the subject Data request — Zentrix Work, or tell your manager.

- Include your name and your account email, and whether you want to see, correct or delete your data.

- We respond within 30 business days at most.

What is deleted, what is kept because of a legal obligation and for how long is explained in the [privacy policy, section 7](https://zentrix.company/en/work/privacy/#c7). Signing out or uninstalling the app does not delete anything from the server.

### Zentrix Check
The security gate · [Zentrix Check →](https://zentrix.company/en/check/)

For almost everything, your first point of contact is your company’s security administrator: they set up the gate phone, create your account and give you your password. For anything else, write to us.

[soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company?subject=Support%20%E2%80%94%20Zentrix%20Check)

Put Support — Zentrix Check in the subject line and tell us your username, your site and what happened. Please don’t send us screenshots of records, plates, invoices or personal data.

### Quick questions

### I don’t have an account. How do I get in?
There is no sign-up: the app is only for the security staff of companies that use Zentrix Check. Your account is created by your company’s security administrator, for the site where you work.

### How is the gate phone set up?
With a QR code the administrator generates in the company’s system. Once scanned, the phone is sealed to that site. Without that code the app does nothing.

### I forgot my PIN
On the PIN screen, tap I forgot my PIN. You sign in again with your username and password and create a new PIN.

### I forgot my password
On the sign-in screen, tap I forgot my password: the security administrator gives you one. The password cannot be changed from the phone.

### There is no signal at the gate
Keep working: what you do is stored encrypted on the phone and sent automatically when the signal returns, without duplicates. The app shows how many items are still waiting. The only thing that needs a signal is fetching what the system says about a new load.

### The gate phone was lost or damaged
Tell the security administrator right away: they can revoke the phone, and the app wipes what it stored as soon as it reconnects. The new phone is set up with another QR code.

### I no longer work at the company or at that site
Your access is closed from the company’s system. The records you signed are kept, because they are the log of what happened at the gate. To request access to or deletion of your personal data, see delete your account or your data.

### Delete your account or your data — Zentrix Check

The app has no sign-up, so accounts aren’t deleted from it either: your company creates and closes them. To request access to, correction or deletion of your data:

- Write to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company?subject=Data%20request%20%E2%80%94%20Zentrix%20Check) with the subject Data request — Zentrix Check, or tell the security administrator.

- Include your name, your username and your site (or, if you don’t use the app, which gate and on what date your vehicle or load went through), and whether you want to see, correct or delete your data.

- We respond within 30 business days at most.

What is deleted, what is kept because of a legal obligation and for how long is in [clause 7 of the privacy policy](https://zentrix.company/en/check/privacy/#c7). Leaving the phone or uninstalling the app doesn’t delete anything from the server, and signed records cannot be changed: if something is wrong, it is corrected with a note.

### Manual

The [guard manual](https://zentrix.company/en/check/docs/) (in Spanish) explains setting up the phone, a truck leaving, receipts, keys, assets and what to do without a signal step by step.

## [Traza — Traceability for documents, products and assets](https://zentrix.company/en/traza/)

Traceability

### Every object, with its identity and its full history.

With Traza, your documents, products, and assets have a verifiable trail: you know where they came from, where they've been, who moved them, and where they are now. Traza has its own website.

[Go to traza.technology (opens in a new tab)](https://traza.technology) [Write to us](mailto:hola@zentrix.company?subject=Traza%3A%20I%27d%20like%20to%20learn%20more)

What it does

### Identify, record, verify, and look up.

For distribution, retail, logistics, services, and document management companies that need to know where everything is and where it's been. QR codes, barcodes, RFID, and integrations, depending on what each case needs.

- 01

### Unique identity
Every object has its origin and its own unique code.

- 02

### Clear accountability
Every movement is recorded along with who made it.

- 03

### Evidence
You verify the location and the evidence for every step.

### Complete history
You see the whole history, physical and digital.

## [Zentrix Work — The app for store and delivery teams](https://zentrix.company/en/work/)

Zentrix Work, the Android app for store teams: work lands on the phone to pick orders, deliver, run delivery routes and take returns during the shift.

For store teams · Android

### Your shift, organized from your phone.

Clock in when you get to the store and the work comes to you: orders to pick, deliveries and returns. When you're done, clock out and your phone is yours again.

[Read the manual](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/)

An order rings. Swipe to take it.

How it works

### A shift with Zentrix Work.

No more watching for messages or asking what's next. The app lets you know, you decide whether to take it, and when you're done, everything is on record.

If it's your first day, the [manual](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/) walks you through every screen with screenshots.

- Clock in at your store Check in and choose what you'll handle today: orders, deliveries or returns.

- An order rings Even with your screen off. You see what it is, its code and how many packages it has.

- Swipe to take it You have 60 seconds. If you can't, tap “I can't” and it goes to a teammate.

- Pick it or deliver it Scan item by item with your camera, package by package.

- Take a break if you need one 5, 10 or 15 minutes without closing your shift or dropping what you started.

- Clock out when you leave And if you forget, the shift closes on its own. Your phone stops ringing.

What it helps you do

### Fewer interruptions, fewer mistakes, more control.

Every feature is built for the real pace of a store: lots of movement, little time and a customer waiting.

- 01

### Pick orders
Pick item by item using your camera as a scanner, and the app tells you if anything is missing before you close.

- 02

### Deliver
At the counter or to the door, package by package, with proof of delivery on the spot.

- 03

### Receive returns
You only take back what support has already approved, so there's no arguing at the counter.

- 04

### Alerts you actually hear
If your phone is on silent, the app tells you and takes you straight to the fix.

- 05

### A shift with a start and an end
You work while you're clocked in. Off shift, nothing interrupts you.

- 06

### Fast, secure sign-in
Sign in once with your email, then with your PIN or fingerprint. Your PIN never leaves your phone.

Use cases

### One shift, three kinds of work.

When you clock in, you choose what you'll handle today. Here's how each one comes in.

- 01

### An order to pick
It rings even with your screen off. Take it with a swipe, pick it by scanning item by item, and the app warns you if anything is missing.

- 02

### A delivery
At the counter or to the door, package by package, with proof of delivery on the spot.

- 03

### A return
You only take back what support has already approved, so there's no arguing at the counter.

Screen by screen

### A shift, from the call to the handover.

Light for working in the sun, dark if you prefer.

Clock in and choose what you handle.

An order rings: swipe to take it.

The queue, most urgent first.

Prepare item by item.

Hand over with the pickup code.

Build your delivery trip.

Receive returns with photos.

Light or dark, your choice.

Real screenshots of the app (in Spanish), with a test store and test customers.

Your phone

### It's your phone, and we treat it that way.

The app runs on your personal phone, so it uses as little as possible and only works while you do.

- Clocked out, it stays quiet. With no active shift, you won't get a single notification.

- Location only during your shift. Never off shift or in the background, and it's deleted after 30 days.

- Easy on your battery. The screen stays on only while a task is open.

- No ads and no advertising ID.

[What data the app uses and why](https://zentrix.company/en/work/privacy/)

### Who it's for

For store staff at companies that use Zentrix Work. There's no sign-up: your manager creates your account with the stores and tasks assigned to you. Anyone can install the app, but without an account it doesn't do anything.

### How to get started

- Ask your manager for access.

- Install Zentrix Work from Google Play.

- Enter the server, your email and your password. Only the first time.

- Create your PIN or use your fingerprint, and you're set.

### Download Zentrix Work

For Android. Questions? Write to us at [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company?subject=Support%20%E2%80%94%20Zentrix%20Work).

[Support](https://zentrix.company/en/support/#work)
